B. The verse contrasts the wasteful luxury behind the "red lacquered gates" (where wine sours and meat rots) with the frozen, starving poor lying dead outside, highlighting the stark inequality between rich and poor (around 24:42–24:55).

This verse is from "Spring Prospect" (春望), written while Du Fu was a captive in the ruined capital during the An Lushan rebellion (spring 756, after the capital fell). His wife was still alive then (he wrote "Moonlit Night" to her during the same captivity), the Tang dynasty had not fallen, and he had already served at court. His infant son had died earlier (winter 755) at Fengxian — but a baby daughter was born much later in Changsha, after this verse.

C. His wife was still alive when he wrote this (as shown by the contemporaneous poem "Moonlit Night" addressed to her), so the verse was written before she died.
